steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'State' requires a brief factual answer without explanation; just give the fact or definition directly.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Describe' requires saying what happens or what a process is, without explaining why it happens.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Explain' requires giving reasons — say what happens and why, linking cause and effect in your answer.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: 'Compare' requires stating similarities and differences between two or more things; use comparative language.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between 'state' and 'explain' in an exam question? | Q: A question asks you to 'compare half-wave and full-wave rectification'. What should your answer include? | Q: How should you approach a 'calculate' question worth 3 marks?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: 'State' needs only a brief factual answer with no reasoning; 'explain' requires you to give reasons, linking cause and effect. | Both similarities (both convert AC to DC using diodes) and differences (full-wave uses both half-cycles, half-wave only one; full-wave has higher output and less ripple). | Write the formula (1 mark), substitute the correct values (1 mark), and give the final numerical answer with correct units (1 mark).

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Underline the command word and the key subject in each question before you start writing. For 'explain' questions, use 'because', 'therefore' or 'due to' to clearly link cause and effect. In 'compare' answers, use a structured format: point about A, then matching point about B, for each feature. For 'calculate' questions, always show your working — marks are awarded for the method, not just the answer. Match the length of your answer to the marks: 1 mark = one sentence; 4 marks = four developed points.
